items.summary: Figma walks through a workflow where project context becomes a plan using Specs and its agent. It shows how the company expects designers to brief and steer the agent.
items.whyItMatters: Try structuring your brief as a spec before handing work to an agent.

items.summary: Nielsen Norman Group tests whether AI can produce good designs starting from raw user research data. Written by named researchers, it adds evidence to a debate that is mostly opinion.
items.whyItMatters: Shows where AI synthesis helps and where you still need to check it.

items.summary: Lovable reflects on two years of the product and who it has opened app building to. A company retrospective rather than a release.
items.whyItMatters: Context on where prompt-to-app tools are heading.

items.summary: Figma profiles how the 1Password team uses Figma Make in its design work. It is a vendor-published case study focused on communicating trust in the product.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete example of Make in a security-sensitive product team.

items.summary: Lovable adds a way to explore several ideas in parallel without changing the live version of a project. It targets the risk of breaking something while iterating.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you branch design explorations without touching production.

items.summary: A designer offers a survival guide for dealing with low-quality AI-generated design work in teams. It is a practitioner opinion piece.
items.whyItMatters: Practical framing for pushing back on weak AI output.

items.summary: An essay on what AI has displaced in design and product work while organizations focus on productivity measures. Opinion with no new data in the title.
items.whyItMatters: A prompt to question which practices you are quietly losing.

items.summary: The Verge reports on vibe-coding spreading to consumer gadgets beyond the laptop and phone. A reported feature from a named journalist.
items.whyItMatters: Signals interface design work expanding to new hardware surfaces.

items.summary: Creative Bloq looks at how Adobe frames its AI tools for creatives and how the tools have changed since it started. Secondhand reporting by a named writer.
items.whyItMatters: Useful read on how a major vendor positions AI to designers.

items.summary: An opinion piece arguing prototypes are the strongest form of specification, especially when AI can produce them quickly.
items.whyItMatters: Supports the case for prototyping over documents in AI workflows.

items.summary: Canva has added a switch that lets users turn off AI features in its tools, according to Fast Company. It responds to creative-community pushback.
items.whyItMatters: A product pattern to watch: opt-out controls for AI features.

items.summary: A designer tests whether AI can build a good design system and reports the results from their own trial.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a first-hand data point before you try it on your own system.

items.summary: Jakob Nielsen's weekly roundup of short UX commentary, touching AI prompts and permission requests.
items.whyItMatters: Skim for quick takes on AI interaction patterns.

items.summary: Creative Bloq covers Canva's AI off switch as a response to creatives' backlash. It overlaps with the broader coverage of the same change.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how designer sentiment is shaping tool settings.
